sourceOperator.localApplicationDomain: 0<q<qStar, where the listed original source fields are defined.
sourceOperator.globalDefinition: Apply (10.4) on the original local domain and extend it identically by zero outside. The entire cutoff support lies in q<qStar/2, so the two definitions agree on an open overlap.
sourceOperator.divergenceIdentity: div curl(c*A)=0 and div(c*B_e_theta)=r^-1 partial_theta(c*B)=0, using the same original axisymmetric B and theta-independent cutoff.
sourceOperator.zeroBranchProof: Inside the original local domain, c=0 and all spatial cutoff derivatives vanish, so every operator coefficient is zero. Outside that domain the global definition is identically zero; no undefined local field is evaluated or multiplied by zero.
sourceOperator.plateauProof: c=1 and grad(c)=0 give the original curl(A)+B_e_theta and the same p_loc, with no omitted commutator.

initialZeroInterval.reason: The temporal cutoff and all its derivatives vanish.

sourceExistenceTheoremApplication.choice: Choose qbig=qBig=2^(-(ell0+4)), a permitted smaller domain inside the explicitly sufficient common6 threshold.
sourceExistenceTheoremApplication.finalDomainIdentification: Proposition9.9 p114 applies its summation lemma with qStar=qbig and shrinks the earlier local thresholds to this common value.
sourceExistenceTheoremApplication.whyLaterStageConstantsDoNotShrinkIt: Lemma9.7 p112 fixes all inverse coefficients and denominators at the primary construction. Later inputs may be arbitrary size; finite derivative losses change constants only.

sourceDomain.zeroExtension: The exact operator is applied on the local source domain. Its support lies strictly inside, and the identically zero outside definition agrees on an open overlap.

flatSeams.conclusion: The captured cutoff and its first four derivatives agree with their constant extensions at both seams. This supplies more derivatives than the force/divergence identities use.
